note: The exchange and interconnection register of the hosted deployment (48.1-01, D-10; CA-3, CA-9, SA-9(2)). One entry per exchange: what crosses, between whom, how it is protected and which code does it. Each entry says only what its implementedBy code does; a planned entry names the plan or phase that builds it. agreement stays 'To be completed by your organization' until your organization records its agreement reference. After any change run `node compliance/src/cli.ts hosted-docs --write` and commit docs/security/hosted-interconnections.md; CI's docs job fails while they differ, and also when a deploy module (tests excluded) calls one of the six signing helpers of deploy/bundle/lib/cosign.mjs and deploy/bundle/signed-file.mjs (signFile, verifySignedFile, signBlob, verifyBlob, signImage, verifyImage) without an exchange naming it; signing by any other means is not detected. operatorJurisdiction and location (48.4 D-08) describe the far end, the end away from the site that reads the register: the ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code of the legal seat of whoever operates it (org when your organization does) and where it is (site when inside the site); unknown when the register cannot know, such as where HQ or another site is, which each site states in its own sovereignty declaration.

exchanges.title: Offline bundle
exchanges.data: Every image of the stack by digest, the vendored charts, the pinned tools (RKE2, helm, cosign, hauler) and the deploy tree (realm, policies, values, local charts, node files and scripts), listed with their digests in manifest.json. No personal information.
exchanges.format: A hauler store archive with manifest.json (sterling-bundle/1) and its Sigstore signature bundle beside it, carried on media or copied.
exchanges.protection: manifest.json is signed with your organization's cosign key, and every image is re-signed with the same key at build. At the site, check.mjs verifies the manifest signature, the archive SHA-256 and every item digest with the public key from the install media before anything is loaded; import.mjs verifies every image signature again in the site registry.
exchanges.frequency: The first install and every update (an update is a newer bundle).
exchanges.agreement: To be completed by your organization

exchanges.title: Person and passkey export
exchanges.data: Each named person's username, email, first and last name, enabled and email-verified flags, and their WebAuthn passwordless credential records (credential id, public key, AAGUID, sign count, attestation format, transports). No private key leaves the person's authenticator; OpenBao Transit keys are not in this file.
exchanges.format: A sterling-users/1 JSON file with its Sigstore signature bundle beside it.
exchanges.protection: Signed with your organization's cosign key. The import verifies the signature with the public key from the install media and refuses an unknown format, an unread feature in requires, another relying-party id or a credential that is not passwordless WebAuthn, all before any Keycloak call.
exchanges.frequency: When a person moves to or is enrolled at another site.
exchanges.agreement: To be completed by your organization

exchanges.title: Site intermediate certificate request
exchanges.data: The certificate signing request of the site's pki_int intermediate (its public key and the site's names). The key is made and kept in OpenBao.
exchanges.format: A PEM certificate signing request with its Sigstore signature bundle beside it.
exchanges.protection: Signed with your organization's cosign key so HQ knows which site sent it; HQ's offline root signs it in the key ceremony.
exchanges.frequency: At install and at each intermediate renewal.
exchanges.agreement: To be completed by your organization

exchanges.title: Signed site intermediate certificate
exchanges.data: The site's intermediate CA certificate issued by HQ's offline root. No private key.
exchanges.format: A PEM certificate file with its Sigstore signature bundle beside it.
exchanges.protection: Signed with your organization's cosign key. The import verifies the signature, that the certificate is a CA certificate issued and signed by the HQ root from the install media and that it is valid now, before any OpenBao call or file write.
exchanges.frequency: At install and at each intermediate renewal.
exchanges.agreement: To be completed by your organization

exchanges.title: Certificate revocation list
exchanges.to: sites and clients that trust it
exchanges.data: The revocation list of the site's pki_int intermediate: serial numbers and revocation times. No personal information.
exchanges.format: A PEM revocation list with its Sigstore signature bundle beside it.
exchanges.protection: Signed with your organization's cosign key; the import verifies it with the public key from the install media before writing anything. It stays valid for crlExpiry, which must outlast the time media takes to arrive.
exchanges.frequency: On each revocation and before the list expires.
exchanges.agreement: To be completed by your organization

exchanges.title: Hub sealed bundle files
exchanges.data: Sealed entries of shared staff projects carried between hubs that are not connected.
exchanges.format: Sealed bundle files as the Phase 34 design defines them.
exchanges.protection: Sealed and signed as the Phase 34 design defines; the register is completed when that code lands.
exchanges.frequency: When a disconnected hub or site exchanges project entries.
exchanges.agreement: To be completed by your organization

exchanges.title: Site evidence export
exchanges.data: Allow-listed deployment facts (settings, counts and versions) read by collect.sh; names, realm contents, secrets and log text stay at the site. Also how a disconnected edge site reports to HQ.
exchanges.format: A signed JSON envelope in the extension's signed-payload format, purpose site export.
exchanges.protection: Ed25519 signature by the site's export key, from a key file or an external signer such as an HSM; the reader refuses an export that does not verify.
exchanges.frequency: At least weekly, inside the 7-day evidence window.
exchanges.agreement: To be completed by your organization

exchanges.title: Model servers
exchanges.to: model servers your organization's signed policy lists
exchanges.data: The prompts and context a person sends and the model's replies; this can include project content up to the level the policy allows for that server.
exchanges.format: HTTPS requests to each listed model server.
exchanges.protection: TLS to the server. Pods reach only the addresses in egressAllow (sterling-network), and sessions use only the servers in modelServers.
exchanges.agreement: To be completed by your organization

exchanges.title: Site mail server
exchanges.data: Passwordless registration links that an administrator sends to a person's email address.
exchanges.protection: STARTTLS to the site's own mail server; the realm sends from the site's own address.
exchanges.frequency: When an administrator sends a registration link.
exchanges.agreement: To be completed by your organization

exchanges.title: Operating system repository
exchanges.data: Operating system packages, such as container-selinux for the RKE2 SELinux package. No site data.
exchanges.format: Packages from the site's mirror of the OS vendor's repository.
exchanges.protection: Packages signed by the OS vendor and checked by the package manager; the site supplies and runs the mirror.
exchanges.frequency: At install and when the site patches its nodes.
exchanges.agreement: To be completed by your organization

exchanges.title: GitHub Container Registry to the HQ build host
exchanges.data: Our built and released images, pulled by their recorded digests. No site data.
exchanges.protection: Pulled by digest over TLS, signed with the release key in the container-release environment when published, and re-signed with your organization's key at bundle build. A published digest enters the image lock only after its signature verifies (deploy/bundle/record-digests.mjs), and the workbench only from the Release workflow's GHCR repository.
exchanges.agreement: To be completed by your organization

exchanges.title: Open VSX mirror
exchanges.data: Requests for extensions by name and version, and the extension packages. No project content.
exchanges.format: HTTPS to the site's own Open VSX mirror.
exchanges.protection: TLS to the mirror the site names; sessions fetch extensions only from there.
exchanges.frequency: When a person installs or updates an extension.
exchanges.agreement: To be completed by your organization

exchanges.title: Smart card revocation checks
exchanges.data: The serial number of a smart card certificate being checked. Off unless the site turns on smart card sign-in.
exchanges.format: OCSP over HTTP to a local responder, or a CRL file refreshed on a schedule.
exchanges.protection: The OCSP answers are signed by the responder; the CRL is signed by its issuer.
exchanges.frequency: At each smart card sign-in, when that sign-in is on.
exchanges.agreement: To be completed by your organization

exchanges.title: Sign-in through HQ
exchanges.data: An OpenID Connect sign-in at HQ for a person who already exists at the edge site (linked by email). Off by default.
exchanges.protection: TLS; the client secret is a Secret at the edge site, never in the site file; HQ's first sign-in only links an existing person, and signing always needs a fresh ceremony with a key registered at the edge.
exchanges.frequency: At sign-in, when the edge is linked to HQ.
exchanges.agreement: To be completed by your organization

exchanges.title: Site time source
exchanges.format: NTP (chrony), optionally with Network Time Security; or a reference clock attached to a node (PHC, SHM or SOCK).
exchanges.protection: Every node's chrony.conf is generated from the site file and names only the site's own sources (no pool, no allow, command port off); NTS trusts the site CA when time.nts is on; with two or more sources chrony needs two to agree. The node install refuses a clock that is not synchronised, follows its own local clock or exceeds time.maxClockErrorMs, before RKE2 is installed, and the install preflight refuses the same on the import host.
exchanges.agreement: To be completed by your organization
